blocking_findings: The footer does not preserve the required epistemic taxonomy. It collapses lemma, proposition, theorem, corollary, and new result into “proved result,” while omitting axiom and the explicit new-result category. Its universal statement that “Every claim is labeled” is also broader than the evidence presented on the page.

The page advertises “machine-checked representative formal artifacts” but provides no links to Proofs.lean, Core.hs, formal.json, or an explanation of their deliberately limited scope. Visitors therefore cannot inspect the evidence supporting the claim.

The website provides no source-grounding or receipt interface: the paper cards expose only PDFs, with no links to LaTeX sources, review records, build receipts, hashes, or claim identifiers. The existing website receipt verifies file hashes only; it does not record link, responsive-layout, accessibility, security, or rendered-page checks.
required_changes: Replace the footer with wording that enumerates the exact categories: definition, axiom, assumption, conjecture, lemma, proposition, theorem, corollary, interpretation, empirical statement, established physical result, and new result. Avoid claiming universal compliance unless backed by an auditable claim ledger.

Add inspectable links for formal/lean/Proofs.lean, formal/haskell/Core.hs, and receipts/formal.json. State that these artifacts check finite algebraic and bookkeeping shadows and do not formalize the differential geometry or physical realization.
Add a provenance or verification section linking the LaTeX sources, relevant reviews, and build receipts, including the corrected synthesis and its S-P1 and S-N3 claims.

Run and record deployment-layout link checks for all four PDF URLs. The local targets exist and their hashes match latex.json, but the ../papers/... URLs require the deployed web root to include the sibling papers directory.
Make repeated “Read PDF” links uniquely named for assistive technology, for example “Read Compositional Systems PDF.”
Use an absolute deployed URL for og:image and add basic Open Graph description metadata before deployment.
Extend receipts/website.json, or add a separate receipt, to record the deployed URL, HTTP status of each link, responsive viewport checks, accessibility checks, and security-header checks.
counterexamples: A visitor following the claim about machine-checked artifacts cannot reach either formal artifact from the website; only the four PDFs are linked.
If only the website directory is published as the hosting root, every ../papers/pdf/... link resolves outside that root and returns 404.
The synthesis distinguishes S-N3 specifically as a “New result claimed by this work,” whereas the website footer erases that distinction under the generic phrase “proved result.”

claim_assessments.explanation: All four local PDF targets exist, are valid six-page PDF 1.7 files, and their SHA-256 hashes match receipts/latex.json. Deployment reachability remains unverified.
receipts/formal.json reports verified=true and its hashes match the final Lean and Haskell files, but the website neither links those files nor states the limited scope of their checks.
topic-workers.json records separate topic tasks, but the public phrase “independently researched” is undefined and has no visible provenance link.
The footer collapses and omits categories that the governing epistemic contract requires to remain distinct.
The HTML contains no mathematical notation or math-rendering library. Mathematical content is delegated to the linked PDFs, whose text extraction confirms the corrected S-P1 and S-N3 statements.

The stylesheet uses a fluid maximum-width layout, clamp-based heading size, auto-fit cards, and a narrow-screen media rule. No obvious static overflow defect was found, although no browser-based viewport receipt was supplied.
The page contains no scripts, forms, inline event handlers, or remote dependencies. Deployment security headers cannot be assessed from the supplied static files.
receipts/website.json hashes match all three website files, but status=ok is not accompanied by evidence for link checking, accessibility, responsive rendering, or deployed HTTP behavior.
